findings: The November 7, 2026 parent URL is a variant index with six links: hosted Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents, Direct API, iOS, and Android (new raw lines 5–20). Mobile links add discoverability beyond the four inlined May 6, 2026 variants (old raw lines 8–10, 87–94, 570–574, 1160–1164); none of these linked implementations were read as November authority.

The May guide describes single-use 7–120 day terms and customer authorization at SeQura with redirection back to the merchant. Its Checkout routes require EUR and same-currency line items, use payment mode, and exclude setup and subscription modes. Hosted manual Checkout builds on an existing Checkout integration and adds sequra to payment_method_types, while the Checkout Sessions API on Elements creates the Session on the server, returns its client secret, and confirms from Checkout on the client (old raw lines 10–48, 95–130, 153–159, 186–196, 244–253, 488–527).

In May Elements with Payment Intents and Direct API the server creates the PaymentIntent, using a server-decided amount for Elements, and passes only the client secret for confirmation. The examples distinguish customer_account (Accounts v2) from customer (Customers v1). PaymentIntent confirmation has return_url, and optional server-side manual redirect uses requires_action and next_action.redirect_to_url. Verify intent status after return and use payment_intent.succeeded for completion workflows (old raw lines 799–934, 1076–1089, 1179–1204, 1287–1362).

Optional manual PaymentIntent capture uses capture_method=manual, proceeds to requires_capture after successful authorization and then an explicit capture request; otherwise Stripe cancels after seven days and emits payment_intent.canceled. In the sandbox the user can approve or decline on the test page; live redirects to SeQura (old raw lines 1094–1146, and 564–568 for Checkout Sessions).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The old filename ends in 2025, but its fetched header is May 6, 2026 (old raw lines 1–4). The November 7, 2026 index is separate evidence of navigation only (new raw lines 1–20).

Retain the May route-specific safeguards: single-use and 7–120 days, checkout eligibility and same-currency line items, payment-only modes, route-specific redirect URLs, payment result verification, sandbox/live distinction, and optional seven-day PaymentIntent capture with cancellation (old raw lines 16–48, 95–130, 564–568, 927–934, 1076–1158 and 1287–1362).

Keep the existing Stripe BNPL concept's reciprocal source route (concept lines 262–269) and add a discoverable summary-to-concept and related overview route. Retain the linked May raw lines 25–27 of the current source and add a distinct November index route.
conflicts: The May Checkout compatibility sections say supported business locations Europe (old raw lines 18–30 and 95–107), while the May Direct API currency mapping lists only EUR: ES (old raw lines 1376–1378) and the separate May method overview explicitly lists ES as the Stripe account business location (raw/stripe-sequra-2025.md lines 52–56). Preserve this route-specific wording without treating it as an eligibility expansion.

The May acceptance description gives 7–120 day terms (old raw lines 16 and 1164); the separate May method overview describes Pay in 3 interest-free or up to 12 installments (raw/stripe-sequra-2025.md lines 1–8). Duration in days and installment count are different measures, and the evidence does not reconcile their product scope. Current source line 19 treats them too strongly as mutually exclusive.

Current source lines 13 and 17 overgeneralize return_url. The May hosted Checkout example uses success_url (old raw lines 45–70), Checkout Sessions Elements examples use return_url containing CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID (old raw lines 153–159 and 186–196), and PaymentIntent confirmation uses return_url (old raw lines 927–934 and 1287–1356). Current lines 13 and 21 should also scope the optional seven-day window to PaymentIntent manual capture.
contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-sequra-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-sequra-accept-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-sequra-accept-payment.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sequra/accept-a-payment`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sequra/accept-a-payment documents a six-link variant selection at new raw lines 5–20. Its four web routes and two Mobile links are navigation. The May 6, 2026 implementation in old raw lines 8–48, 95–130, 153–196, 799–934, 1094–1146 and 1287–1362 covers single-use SeQura, hosted Checkout and Elements, same-currency EUR Checkout line items in payment mode only, server creation of a Checkout Session or PaymentIntent, and client confirmation using the corresponding object and secret. The buyer authorizes with SeQura and returns, then the merchant verifies payment status. On the optional PaymentIntent manual-capture branch, successful authorization reaches requires_capture, capture is explicit, and the uncaptured Intent is canceled after seven days. The prior capture also distinguishes test-page approval or decline from live redirection. source-stripe-sequra-accept-payment.md needs to scope return_url to the applicable Elements or PaymentIntent path, preserve hosted Checkout's success_url example and identify the seven-day rule as optional PaymentIntent capture.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sequra/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 9–20 replace inline content with six navigation links, including iOS and Android, and do not establish a substantive payment change or removed web pathway relative to the May 6, 2026 dated material in old raw lines 8–48, 87–112, 570–575 and 1160–1164. Keep May implementation and November routing separately in source-stripe-sequra-accept-payment.md with the reciprocal stripe-bnpl concept route. Preserve the May Checkout Europe label, Direct API EUR: ES mapping (old raw lines 1376–1378) and the related May overview's Spain business listing as differing scopes. Preserve the 7–120 day description alongside the overview’s installment counts. Explain the historic return and optional capture boundaries using old raw lines 45–70, 153–196, 927–934 and 1094–1141. The November index does not establish eligibility, payment success, deprecation or mobile SDK behavior.
